motion.name: spring
motion.purpose: Deliberate playful overshoot, scoped to small press and pop interactions: button/chip/key press (0.2-0.25s), Add button and card hover (0.3-0.35s), switch thumb, match-number pop and toast entry (0.45-0.5s). Not for large moves or anything being read.

motion.name: sheen

motion.name: state-fade
motion.purpose: Colour, background and border changes on hover and focus.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All motion collapses under prefers-reduced-motion; foil scratch resolves instantly.

components.css: .ds-btn { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; gap:8px; min-height:50px; padding:0 20px; border:0; border-radius:999px; font-family:'Bricolage Grotesque Variable', system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight:700; font-size:16px; cursor:pointer; box-shadow: inset 0 -3px 0 oklch(0 0 0 / 0.18); transition: transform 0.25s var(--spring, cubic-bezier(0.34,1.56,0.64,1)), background-color 0.2s; } .ds-btn:hover { transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-btn:active { transform: translateY(1px) scale(0.97); box-shadow: inset 0 -1px 0 oklch(0 0 0 / 0.18); } .ds-btn:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--lime, oklch(0.91 0.19 124)); outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--coral, oklch(0.72 0.19 30)); color: var(--card-ink, oklch(0.2 0.07 295)); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--coral-hi, oklch(0.77 0.17 34)); }

components.css: .ds-strips { display:grid; gap:8px; width:200px; } .ds-fstrip { display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; min-height:38px; padding:0 10px; border-radius:12px; font-family:'Bricolage Grotesque Variable', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size:13px; font-weight:800; font-stretch:85%; letter-spacing:0.02em; text-transform:uppercase; } .ds-fstrip-foil { color: oklch(0.32 0.07 295 / 0.85); background: linear-gradient(115deg, #c9ccd8 0%, #f4c9ec 22%, #c3edf7 44%, #e7f7c0 64%, #f6dcc0 82%, #cfd2de 100%); background-size:220% 100%; animation: ds-sheen 6s ease-in-out infinite alternate; } .ds-fstrip-called { background: var(--card-ink, oklch(0.2 0.07 295)); color: var(--mint, oklch(0.87 0.13 172)); } .ds-fstrip-won { background: var(--card-ink, oklch(0.2 0.07 295)); color: var(--lime, oklch(0.91 0.19 124)); } @keyframes ds-sheen { to { background-position: 100% 0; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-fstrip-foil { animation:none; } }

narrative.overview:
Every ticket is a punchy, printed scratch card dealt onto a deep night-violet table. The ground is dark, quiet and dotted with faint confetti; everything the owner touches is loud card stock in hot coral, cobalt, acid lime, tangerine or bubblegum, each with its own ink. The one real material is holographic silver foil: a pastel conic-style sheen with sparkle grain that covers what is still unknown and gets scratched away when a number is called.

The system is built for a crowded hall and one hand. Numbers are huge, condensed and tabular; targets are fat and pill-shaped or candy-chunky; depth is a bevel you can press. Motion is playful but short: things pop, deal and spring back, and then sit still so a number can be read at arm's length.

Grey list rows and the premium-wallet look are rejected for this world: tickets are never rendered as quiet table rows or as sober leather-and-gold wallet passes.
keyCharacteristics: Dark night-violet ground with a 26px confetti-dot pattern; colour lives on the cards, not the chrome.
Five card-stock tones assigned per ticket number, each paired with its own ink.
Holographic foil as the status material: pending is foil, called and won are the foil scratched off.
Bricolage Grotesque throughout; condensed weight 800 for numerals and the wordmark, normal width for UI copy.
Candy depth: inset top highlight plus inset bottom bevel that compresses on press.
Springy overshoot on small press and pop interactions only.

rules.name: The Colour Lives On The Card Rule
rules.body: Saturated tones belong to cards, the Add button, and status signals. Chrome (top bar, sheets, chips, keypad) stays in the violet neutrals.

rules.name: The Tone Carries Its Ink Rule
rules.body: A card tone is always set as a pair: background tone plus its ink (card ink on coral, lime, tangerine, bubblegum; chalk ink on cobalt). Never put text on a tone without its paired ink.

rules.name: The Two Signals Rule
rules.body: Lime means yours / won; mint means called. Do not swap them or use either decoratively on the ground.

rules.name: The Squeezed Numeral Rule
rules.body: Every ticket number, called number and key cap is weight 800 at reduced width (75-85%). Width does the shouting; never add size beyond the clamps to make a number louder.

rules.name: The Uppercase Is Foil Rule
rules.body: Uppercase is reserved for text printed on a strip or the reveal panel (DRAW PENDING, CALLED, IT'S YOURS). UI copy stays sentence case.

rules.name: The Press-The-Bevel Rule
rules.body: Anything chunky that can be pressed shows a bottom bevel at rest and loses most of it on `:active`, with a 1-3px downward move. Flat elements (chips, icon buttons, fields) don't fake one.

dos: **Do** assign a card tone from the five card-stock colours by ticket number and always pair it with its ink.
**Do** use the holographic foil (gradient plus sparkle grain) for anything not yet revealed, and scratch it off to show called or won.
**Do** set every number in Bricolage Grotesque weight 800 at 75-85% width with tabular figures.
**Do** give pressable chunky elements a bottom bevel that compresses on press.
**Do** use the spring easing (`cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1)`) for small press and pop interactions: buttons, chips, keys, the Add button, switch thumbs, card hover, the match pop and toasts.
**Do** keep touch targets at 44px minimum, and 50px+ for primary actions.
**Do** honour reduced motion: animations and transitions collapse to near zero.
donts: **Don't** render tickets as grey list rows or in a premium-wallet register.
**Don't** put saturated card tones on chrome (top bar, sheet backgrounds, keypad).
**Don't** use lime and mint interchangeably; lime is yours / won, mint is called.
**Don't** use the spring overshoot on large moves or anything the owner is waiting to read.
**Don't** set UI copy in uppercase; uppercase belongs on strips and the reveal panel.
